canonical_name: Concurrency Kit 0.7.2 -- lock-free data structures, spinlocks with backoff, hazard pointers (Samy Al Bahra)
lineage: A C library of the classic concurrent-memory-model machinery: ck_spinlock (ticket, MCS, CLH, anderson, hclh; with ck_backoff exponential backoff), ck_ring/ck_fifo/ck_stack lock-free structures, ck_hp hazard pointers and ck_epoch safe memory reclamation (2011-). Reference rivals: liblfds, Boost.Lockfree.
entry_points: include/ck_backoff.h (ck_backoff_eb: exponential backoff), include/spinlock/*.h, include/ck_ring.h, include/ck_hp.h; regressions/<module>/validate
upstream_docs: doc/ man pages in the tree; Al Bahra, Nonblocking Algorithms and Scalable Multicore Programming, ACM Queue 2013

human_capability_summary.built_to: let many threads share structures without a global lock, and make contending threads back off instead of hammering a cache line
human_capability_summary.pressure: cache-line contention, memory reordering, reclamation while readers are live
human_capability_summary.success_means: linearizable operations under contention; no lost updates; freed memory never dereferenced

human_environmental_pressure: resource contention (cache lines, locks), memory-model weakness, reclamation hazards
human_failure_condition: lost updates, torn reads, use-after-free, or a convoy of spinning threads starving the holder
behavioral_entry_point: run a spinlock validate binary with more threads than cores; switch spinlock implementation (ticket vs MCS vs anderson) and compare

lineage_relations.to: Mellor-Crummey & Scott 1991 (MCS lock); Michael 2004 (hazard pointers); Fraser 2004 (epoch reclamation)

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run concurrencykit-0.7.2
nyx_handoff.what_humans_used_it_for: let many threads share structures without a global lock, and make contending threads back off instead of hammering a cache line
